about: Materials every site is composed from. Each property carries its source and the quoted line, or is marked assumed or derived with the reasoning. Values are a representative point inside a range; sweeps draw from the range. Units: m/s, kg/m3.

sharafeldin2019.citation: Sharafeldin, S. M., Essa, K. S., Youssef, M. A. S., Karsli, H., Diab, Z. E., Sayil, N. (2019). Shallow geophysical techniques to investigate the groundwater table at the Great Pyramids of Giza, Egypt. Geoscientific Instrumentation, Methods and Data Systems 8, 29-43.
sharafeldin2019.note: 26 seismic refraction profiles on the Giza plateau and its eastern edge (Sphinx, Valley Temple, mastaba field).

gpg.citation: UBC Geophysical Inversion Facility. Seismic Velocities of Rocks and Various Materials. Geophysics for Practicing Geoscientists (GPG), table_seismic_velocity.
gpg.note: Textbook ranges, CC-BY. The basalt S-wave entry reads '2800 - 2400' in the source; recorded verbatim, not used.

gamal2024.citation: Gamal, M. A., Abdelfattah, M., Maher, G. (2024). Investigation and monitoring of rotational landslides in El Mokkattam plateau Egypt, using integrated geological and geophysical techniques. Heliyon 10, e36545.

rho.note: Near-surface air; a void is simulated as a traction-free cavity, so this value is not used by the elastic solver.

dry-sand-giza.name: Dry sand and gravel (Giza surface layer)

vp.quote: The topmost layer exhibits a velocity range of 500–1000 m s−1, and thicknesses of 3 and 6 m are correlated with dry sand and gravels.

vs.note: Giza-specific S-wave speeds are not reported by the refraction study; the textbook dry-sand range is used.

limestone-fractured.name: Fractured, wet limestone and marl (Giza second layer)

vp.quote: The second layer shows a velocity range between 1200 and 2500 m s−1 at 8 m to more than 30 m thick. … the upper part of this layer shows a relatively lower velocity due to water saturation and fractures.

vs.note: Vp divided by Vp/Vs ≈ 2.3, the ratio of the extremes measured on fractured Mokattam limestone by gamal2024 (P 850–2000 m/s, S 400–800 m/s).
vs.quote: the lowest P-wave seismic velocity was found to be 850 m/s at the sliding zone … the highest … about 2000 m/s … The lowest S-wave seismic velocity was found to be between 400 and 580 m/s … the highest S-wave seismic velocity is about 800 m/s

vp.quote: The third layer shows a higher velocity that ranges between 2800 and 3800 m s−1, which can be correlated with the limestone and dolomite of the Mokattam Formation.

vs.note: Vp divided by Vp/Vs ≈ 1.8, the ratio implied by the textbook limestone ranges (P 3500–6000, S 2000–3300 m/s).

vp.note: Jointed blocks with mortar and gaps: slower than intact limestone. No measured value has been found; to be replaced when one is.
